assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction turned electron microscopy from a technique limited by the lens by itself into one that routinely resolves individual atomic columns and, with spectroscopy, single-atom chemistry and bonding. It is a clear invention with an immediate, field-wide effect on physics, materials science, catalysis and nanoscience, and the prize is for a discovery or invention rather than lifetime achievement. My own field is close, so I judge the impact from direct knowledge of how much the instrument changed what can be measured.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector concepts, Haider led the first working hexapole corrector for TEM, and Krivanek built the quadrupole-octupole corrector for STEM. Those three are the decisive named contributions. Others, such as Urban and Batson who demonstrated early working correctors, are not among the supplied credited names, so a three-person award from this list is defensible but leaves a visible credit question.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Correctors have been commercial for roughly two decades and are used in laboratories worldwide, the achieved resolution is independently verified, and the recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize committee views instrument development in electron optics as physics rather than technique; precedent such as Ruska in 1986 supports it.
Credit for the first demonstrated correctors may extend beyond the three supplied names.
I work in this community, so I cannot claim full independence in judging relative contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainty near 10^-18, which is a qualitative gain in precision measurement. They allow tests of relativity at the millimetre scale, searches for variation of constants and a likely redefinition of the second. The idea is original, the demonstration is unambiguous and the use is already broad.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and realised the first strontium lattice clock; Ye's group pushed the accuracy and coherence to the 10^-18 regime. Two names give a clean allocation. Contributions from other groups in ion and optical-clock development, and from frequency-comb work already recognised in 2005, remain adjacent but separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent groups reproduce the performance, comparisons between clocks are routine, and international metrology bodies are acting on the results. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: The line between lattice clocks and the earlier single-ion clock lineage is a judgement call.
The roadmap for the redefinition of the second is not finished.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical identification of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, followed by experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells and three-dimensional materials, created a major field in condensed matter physics. It is conceptually clear and has influenced many materials and device directions.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theoretical proposal and the Z2 classification. Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route, and Zhang is deceased, so the supplied names do not cover every decisive contributor and a fair trio is somewhat contingent.
assessment.maturity: Largely mature: the theory is well established and the 2D and 3D realisations have been confirmed by many groups, though practical applications are still limited.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the HgTe proposal and for the three-dimensional materials work.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize may count against it for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and their experimental observation, together with correlated insulators and superconductivity, opened moiré quantum matter as a platform where interaction strength can be tuned by geometry. It is a new and fast-growing area with strong conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group led the experimental discovery. The first author of the key experimental papers is not among the credited names, which complicates a fair assignment, and a three-person set must balance theory against experiment.
assessment.maturity: Still young. Replication across many groups is strong, but the mechanism behind superconductivity and several correlated states remains debated, so premature recognition is a real risk.
uncertainties: Experimental credit extends to people not on the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision model gives the physical picture behind high-harmonic generation and attosecond pulses, and it underpins a whole field of time-resolved electron dynamics. The 2023 prize recognised attosecond light generation and measurement, so this is the conceptual core behind a field already honoured, and its additional distinct merit has to be argued.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's three-step model is the clearest single origin; Schafer and colleagues' simultaneous work and Lewenstein's quantum-mechanical treatment complete the theoretical picture. Contributors to the strong-field ionisation experiments of the same period are not on the list, so attribution is shared between a classical picture and its quantum formulation.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of confirmation, though the main recognition has partly been delivered by the 2023 prize, which weakens the case for timing.
uncertainties: Division of credit between the semiclassical model and the quantum theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskites introduced a low-cost semiconductor with remarkable optoelectronic properties and drove solar-cell efficiencies up rapidly, an unusually fast rise for a photovoltaic material. The materials physics, including defect tolerance and the structure-property relation, is a rich topic and I would assess it with interest.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised solar cell, Park produced the first solid-state cell with durable efficiency, and Snaith demonstrated meso-superstructured and planar devices. Others contributed film-processing and stability advances, so the allocation among the three is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Active and still maturing: efficiencies are well confirmed, but long-term stability, toxicity and manufacturability are unresolved, so a prize may be early for the device claims.
uncertainties: Device stability is an open question.
Whether the committee sees the key advance as a physics discovery or as device engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-quality hexagonal boron nitride crystals became the standard dielectric and encapsulation layer for van der Waals heterostructures, enabling clean graphene devices, quantum Hall physics and moiré experiments. This is a materials invention with a documented effect on many discoveries, and I judge the crystal quality from the standpoint of an experimentalist who knows what clean interfaces are worth.
assessment.attribution: The crystal growth is concentrated in two people, who supplied the crystals used worldwide, so credit is simple. The difficulty is that the work is enabling and does not itself constitute a discovery of a new phenomenon, which tests the discovery-or-invention wording.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a technique, with wide independent use, but recognition would be for an enabling material rather than a physical effect.
uncertainties: Whether the prize standard is met by an enabling material.
Credit for later heterostructure assembly methods is not covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube detected a flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later associated neutrinos with a blazar and with the Galactic plane, establishing neutrino astronomy as an observational field. It is a significant discovery and technological accomplishment.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the concept and the project, and Spiering was an early leader of the collaboration; the credit sits in a large collaboration in which the supplied two-name set represents leadership rather than a clearly separable personal discovery. Other founders of the field and of the detector design may need consideration.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the diffuse flux is confirmed, though source identification is partial and only a few associations rest on small statistics.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit and the fairness of a two-person set.
Source associations are still statistically limited.
